text: Important to say that CTE doesn't make you kill people. Most people with CTE won't be violent. However, it can reduce inhibitions, essentially, encouraging mood swings and reducing impulse control. What you do with your low mood and impulsivity is still up to you. In that respect it's a lot like being drunk: some drunk people are violent, angry and abusive, while others are quiet and polite, because the drink might take down the social barriers to violence but a lot of people don't have the impulses to violence in the first place (behaviour while drunk is also partially socially learned - we imitate how we see our drunk peers act - but that's a different discussion). I don't know Benoit's story well, but when I read abhout it years ago I did also wonder whether he didn't have a mental illness as well as the dementia - reminds me of someone like Tony Ferguson, who already had the paranoid schizophrenia before he accumulated the brain damage. Of course, if you're already prone to delusions due to untreated mental illness, adding mood swings and impulsivity is a really dangerous combination.
